title: FizzBuzz
domain: Integers 1 through 100; the program prints exactly one line per integer.
description: Print the numbers 1 to 100, replacing multiples of 3 with Fizz, multiples of 5 with Buzz, and multiples of both with FizzBuzz. The Glon implementation is the posted version, divided into ten-row recursive blocks so the 64K interpreter's activation depth is not exceeded.
attribution: Problem and REBOL reference: Rosetta Code, 'FizzBuzz' (https://rosettacode.org/wiki/FizzBuzz). The REBOL listing is the solution shown on that page; the Glon implementation is the posted Glon version.
reference: The 100 expected lines are generated independently by Python's integer modulo rules, not by Glon. The full stdout is compared exactly.
family_note: Rosetta Code challenge; separate from the REBOL Cookbook file-replacement challenge.

resource_probes.observed: exit 1; machine halt after about 83 lines (return-stack exhaustion); no SIN!
resource_probes.note: Control probe demonstrating why rows are divided into ten-row blocks. It is a resource-limit probe, not a correctness case.

known_limitations: A single recursive row over 1..100 reaches about 83 lines and then fail-stops with return-stack exhaustion on the pinned 64K interpreter; this is a machine halt, not a catchable SIN!.
The posted rows implementation succeeds by dividing the range into ten-row blocks, keeping each row's recursion shallow.
The program prints exactly 1..100; extending the upper bound is outside this challenge.

reference_implementation.title: FizzBuzz — REBOL solution shown on Rosetta Code
reference_implementation.notes: Concatenative repeat/case/all implementation with a proper REBOL code header.

rebol.observable_behaviour: Prints FizzBuzz, Fizz, Buzz or the number for 1..100.
rebol.facilities: repeat, copy, case/all, append, mod, mold and print from REBOL 2.
rebol.test_status: The original listing is preserved verbatim as reference source. It was not executed here; there is no REBOL 2 runtime in this repository.

glon.observable_behaviour: Prints the same 100 lines; verified exactly against independently generated expected output.
glon.facilities: Ordinary Glon func/either, arithmetic/comparison, s/print and print; no new primitive or vocabulary.
glon.test_status: 1/1 full-output case passed on the pinned interpreter; the direct 100-row probe records the activation-depth limit.

implementation_comparison.notice: Both listings are application-level programs. REBOL iterates with repeat; Glon recurses in ten-row blocks because its bounded activation resources make a single 100-line recursion fail. Source sizes are descriptive, not a concision claim.
